title: wir — We
description: Practise changing the object with wir: present, future and past.
intro: Every example uses Wir as its subject, meaning we in this file. Uns is translated as each other when it refers back to this plural subject; ourselves/yourselves is also possible in an appropriate context. Keep the subject fixed and vary whom the subject sees or to whom the subject gives the book. Sehen takes an accusative object. Geben takes a dative recipient plus das Buch as the accusative thing. The highlighted key is the object or recipient. English labels: (s) singular, (p) plural, (f) formal.

sections.title: wir — changing the object
sections.explanation: Start with the present-tense accusative and dative lists, then compare the same object choices in Futur I and Perfekt. Short sentences omit final full stops.
sections.rule: Wir sehen + Akkusativ | Wir geben + Dativ + das Buch

entries.explanation: The subject and verb stay fixed. Change the accusative object.

examples.note: Singular feminine: her.
Reciprocal reading: each other. A reflexive ourselves/yourselves/themselves reading is also possible in context.
Plural: them. Same German spelling as her; context distinguishes the meaning.
Formal object or recipient: always capitalized; one or more addressees.

entries.explanation: The subject, verb and das Buch stay fixed. Change only the dative recipient. Ihm is translated as him here, but can also refer to a neuter noun.

examples.note: Masculine or neuter dative; translated him here.

examples.english: We give each other the book
examples.note: Reciprocal reading: each other. A reflexive ourselves/yourselves/themselves reading is also possible in context.
Formal object or recipient: always capitalized; one or more addressees.

entries.explanation: Use werden plus sehen to practise the future tense. The infinitive goes at the end and the object's case stays the same. German also uses the present tense with a future time expression.

examples.note: Singular feminine: her.
Reciprocal reading: each other. A reflexive ourselves/yourselves/themselves reading is also possible in context.
Plural: them. Same German spelling as her; context distinguishes the meaning.
Formal object or recipient: always capitalized; one or more addressees.

entries.explanation: Use werden plus geben to practise the future tense. The infinitive goes at the end and the object's case stays the same. German also uses the present tense with a future time expression.
entries.pattern: Wir werden + Dativ + das Buch + geben

examples.german: Wir werden mir das Buch geben
examples.english: We will give me the book

examples.german: Wir werden dir das Buch geben
examples.english: We will give you (s) the book

examples.german: Wir werden ihm das Buch geben
examples.english: We will give him the book
examples.note: Masculine or neuter dative; translated him here.

examples.german: Wir werden ihr das Buch geben
examples.english: We will give her the book

examples.german: Wir werden uns das Buch geben
examples.english: We will give each other the book
examples.note: Reciprocal reading: each other. A reflexive ourselves/yourselves/themselves reading is also possible in context.

examples.german: Wir werden euch das Buch geben
examples.english: We will give you (p) the book

examples.german: Wir werden ihnen das Buch geben
examples.english: We will give them the book

examples.german: Wir werden Ihnen das Buch geben
examples.english: We will give you (f) the book
examples.note: Formal object or recipient: always capitalized; one or more addressees.

entries.explanation: Use haben plus gesehen for a past event. Perfekt is common in conversation. The English examples use saw; depending on context, have/has seen is also possible. The object's case stays the same.

Plural: them. Same German spelling as her; context distinguishes the meaning.
